bargaining_script: ಇದು ಎಷ್ಟು? (how much?) → ತುಂಬಾ ದುಬಾರಿ! (too pricey!) → ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ (reduce a little) → ರಿಯಾಯಿತಿ ಕೊಡಿ (give a discount) → ಸರಿ, ಪ್ಯಾಕ್ ಮಾಡಿ! (done, pack it!)

classifiers.note: one book — number + noun, no extras
two books — the noun takes the -ಗಳು plural

colors.note: colour words never change for gender

consonants.hint: ng as in sing — almost only in clusters
ny as in canyon — rare alone
soft t, tongue on teeth — like Spanish t
very rare — old words only; just recognise it

counting_note: Kannada has no classifiers — put the number straight before the noun. But the noun itself goes plural with -ಗಳು: ಒಂದು ಪುಸ್ತಕ (one book), ಎರಡು ಪುಸ್ತಕಗಳು (two books), ಮೂರು ರೂಪಾಯಿ (three rupees).

culture.en: The maharaja's palace in Mysuru — lit with a lakh of bulbs on Sundays and through Dasara.
Karnataka's royal festival (Sep–Oct) — the Mysuru procession with caparisoned elephants.
The Vijayanagara empire's boulder-strewn capital — now a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Strong, milky, frothed dabara-to-tumbler — Coorg beans run the state's mornings.
The coast's all-night dance-drama — huge crowns, drums, stories from the epics.

lines.en: Hello! I'm Divya. How are you?
lines.hi: नमस्कार! मैं दिव्या हूँ। आप कैसे हैं?

lines.en: I'm fine, thanks. Where are you from?
lines.hi: मैं ठीक हूँ, धन्यवाद। आप कहाँ से हैं?

lines.en: I'm from Mysuru. Which is your town?
lines.hi: मैं मैसूर से हूँ। आपका शहर कौन-सा है?

lines.en: I'm from Bengaluru. I'm learning Kannada.
lines.hi: मैं बेंगलुरु से हूँ। मैं कन्नड़ सीख रहा हूँ।

lines.en: Give me one masala dosa and one filter coffee.
lines.hi: एक मसाला डोसा और एक फ़िल्टर कॉफ़ी दीजिए।
lines.r: Ondu masāla dose matte ondu philṭar kāphi koḍi.
lines.t: ಒಂದು ಮಸಾಲ ದೋಸೆ ಮತ್ತೆ ಒಂದು ಫಿಲ್ಟರ್ ಕಾಫಿ ಕೊಡಿ.

lines.hi: चटनी-सांबार के साथ लाता हूँ। और कुछ?
lines.r: Chaṭni sāmbār jotege taruttēne. Bēre ēnādarū?
lines.t: ಚಟ್ನಿ ಸಾಂಬಾರ್ ಜೊತೆಗೆ ತರುತ್ತೇನೆ. ಬೇರೆ ಏನಾದರೂ?

lines.en: No, that's enough. How much is the bill?

family.note: also used for any older boy, respectfully
also used for any older girl, respectfully
both sides — add ಅಜ್ಜನವರು for extra respect

gender_note: Kannada has three genders: masculine (ಅವನು, he), feminine (ಅವಳು, she) and neuter (ಅದು — animals, things, babies). Only third-person verbs show gender: ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತಾನೆ/ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತಾಳೆ/ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತದೆ (he/she/it eats). 'I' and 'you' never change: ನಾನು ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತೇನೆ suits every speaker.

greetings.note: works any time of day, for everyone

name: Kannada
negation_note: ಇಲ್ಲ (illa) melts into the verb: ಬರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ (won't come / doesn't come), ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ (don't know), ಮಾಡುವುದಿಲ್ಲ (won't do). Alone, ಇಲ್ಲ just means 'no'. To refuse an offer, ಬೇಡ (bēḍa — 'don't want') is warmer: ಕಾಫಿ ಬೇಡ (no coffee for me, thanks).

postpositions.ex_en: The book is on the table.

present_note: The present is stem + -ಉತ್ತ- + ending: -ಏನೆ (I), -ಈಯೆ (ನೀನು), -ಈರಿ (ನೀವು), -ಆನೆ/-ಆಳೆ/-ಅದೆ (he/she/it), -ಏವೆ (we), -ಆರೆ (they). So ನಾನು ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತೇನೆ (I eat), ನೀವು ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತೀರಿ (you eat, respectful), ಅವರು ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ (they eat). In quick speech the endings blur — listen for the -ಉತ್ತ- core.

quiz.explain: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ (namaskāra) is the respectful Kannada hello — any time of day.
ಧನ್ಯವಾದ (dhanyavāda) is thanks — same Sanskrit root as Hindi धन्यवाद.
ನಿಮ್ಮ ಹೆಸರೇನು? = what's your name — answer ನನ್ನ ಹೆಸರು … (my name is …).
ಕ (ka) is a plain k — ಖ (kha) is the breathy one.
ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು (ippattu) = 20, ಹತ್ತೊಂಬತ್ತು = 19, ಮೂವತ್ತು = 30.
ಐವತ್ತು (aivattu) = 50. ಐದು = 5, ಹದಿನೈದು = 15, ಐನೂರು = 500.
quiz.q: 'ಐವತ್ತು ರೂಪಾಯಿ' on a price tag means…

quiz.explain: ದೋಸೆ — with chutney and sambar — is Karnataka's gift to breakfast.
ರುಚಿ (ruchi) = taste — say it and any cook will beam.
ನನಗೆ ಹಸಿವಾಗಿದೆ = I'm hungry (hunger has come to me).
quiz.q: You're hungry in Mysuru. You say…

quiz.explain: ಎಲ್ಲಿ (elli) = where — the traveller's most useful word.
ಟಿಕೆಟು (ṭikeṭu) = ticket; ಬಾಡಿಗೆ = fare; ನಿಲ್ದಾಣ = station.
ಇಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿ (illi nillisi) = stop here. ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಹೋಗಿ = go slowly.
quiz.q: To make the auto stop here, say…

quiz.explain: ತಿನ್ನುತ್ತೇನೆ never marks gender — it suits every speaker. Only he/she/it verbs differ.
ಅವನು …-ಆನೆ (he), ಅವಳು …-ಆಳೆ (she), ಅದು …-ಅದೆ (it).
quiz.q: How does a man say 'he eats'?

quiz.explain: ತಿಂದನು/ತಿಂದಳು (he/she ate) — the past keeps the gender split.
ನೀವು ಊಟ ಮಾಡಿದಿರಾ? — 'have you eaten?' — is asked like 'how are you', with real warmth.
ಮತ್ತೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ (matte sigōṇa) — literally 'we'll meet again' — the warm goodbye.
ಸುಸ್ವಾಗತ (susvāgata) — the warm Kannada welcome.
ಪುಸ್ತಕ (pustaka) = book — ಲೇಖನಿ is the old word for pen.
ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ (snēhita) = friend — ಗೆಳೆಯ is the casual 'buddy'.
ಇದು ಎಷ್ಟು? = how much is this — then counter with ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿ!
ನಾಳೆ (nāḷe) = tomorrow; ನಿನ್ನೆ (ninne) = yesterday. Don't mix them at the station!

script_note: Kannada's letters are famously round — the script was written with a stylus on palm leaves, and straight lines would have torn the leaf. It runs left to right with no headline bar, and it is beautifully phonetic: each letter is one sound, always. There are 13 vowels (ಅ ಆ ಇ ಈ ಉ ಊ ಋ ಎ ಏ ಐ ಒ ಓ ಔ, plus ಅಂ/ಅಃ for nasalization) and 34 consonants. Letters join into conjuncts (ಒತ್ತಕ್ಷರ): ಕ + ್ + ಣ = ಕ್ಷಣ (kshaṇa, moment). Close cousin of the Telugu script — learn one and the other looks familiar.
